name: Michigan
agency: Michigan Department of State (Secretary of State)
permitAge: 14 years 9 months (Level 1 Learner's License), after Segment 1 of driver education

teen.nightLimit: Level 2: no driving 10 p.m. to 5 a.m. except work, an authorized activity, or with a parent/guardian or designated licensed driver 21+
teen.passengerLimit: Level 2: no more than one passenger under 21, except immediate family (and the same exceptions as the night limit)
teen.phone: Kelsey's Law: Level 1 and Level 2 drivers may not use a cell phone while driving (emergencies excepted). Since June 30, 2023 all drivers: no holding a phone, even when stopped at a light.

bac.adult: 0.08 (0.17 or more is the high-BAC offense)
bac.under21: 0.02 or any bodily alcohol content (zero tolerance)

notes: Level 1 drivers must be with a licensed parent/guardian or, with their permission, a licensed driver 21+.
Level 2 also needs: age 16, Segment 2, skills test, and 90 days with no convictions, civil infractions, suspensions or at-fault crashes. Advance is automatic.
Level 3 at 17 at the earliest, with parental authorization.

Speed (MDOT): 70 mph on limited-access freeways without a posted limit; 75 mph posted on about 600 miles of rural freeway; 55 mph on trunkline and county highways without a posted limit; 25 mph residential subdivision; 15 mph mobile home park.
Move over: for stopped emergency, tow, utility, road-maintenance and garbage vehicles with lights on, move over if possible and slow to at least 10 mph below the posted limit.
Left turn on red onto a one-way street (moving the way you turn) after a full stop, unless a sign forbids it.
School bus on a divided highway: only traffic going the same way as the bus must stop; stop at least 20 feet away.
No-fault state: PIP coverage required; limits changed in 2019-2020 reform (details not confirmed).
Knowledge test: offered in multiple languages (official); exact question count and pass mark conflict in third-party sources (50 questions; 70% vs 80%). Teens take it in Segment 1.
